title: 03. Energy Balance Basics
text: single well-behaved run isn’t proof solver robust – checking across spread random trait combinations :  Real, checked rather assumed: every completed run converges within small, bounded number iterations, well 1 W/m² residual – Scripts/R/ForSCOPE/6-validate_ebal_convergence.R runs check production scale (hundreds runs) row fail outright, tryCatch() around get.SCOPE() right pattern (used throughout series ), since extreme random parameter combination can occasionally cause native/numerical fault rather catchable R-level error.
code:
inputLUT <- read.table(file.path(path_input, "inputs_SCOPE.csv"), header = TRUE, sep = ",") n_check <- 40 LUT_check <- getLUT.SCOPE(inputLUT = inputLUT, nLUT = n_check, setseed = 3)  convergence <- lapply(seq_len(n_check), function(i) {   out <- tryCatch(     invisible(capture.output(       r <- get.SCOPE(LUT = LUT_check[i, ], options.SCOPE = table.with.opts,                       optipar = SCOPEinR::optipar2021.Pro.CX, leaf.model = "fluspect-CX",                       canopy.model = "fourSAIL", get.outputs = "ALL", get.plots = FALSE)[[1]]     )),     error = function(e) NULL   )   if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)   data.frame(iterations = r$iter.ebal$counter,              max_resid = max(abs(c(r$iter.ebal$maxEBercu, r$iter.ebal$maxEBerch, r$iter.ebal$maxEBers)))) }) conv_df <- do.call(rbind, convergence)  cat(nrow(conv_df), "/", n_check, "simulations completed.
") #> 40 / 40 simulations completed. cat("Median iterations to converge:", median(conv_df$iterations), "
") #> Median iterations to converge: 7 cat("Max residual across all runs:", round(max(conv_df$max_resid), 4), "W/m2
") #> Max residual across all runs: 0.9988 W/m2 hist(conv_df$iterations, breaks = 10, col = "#2E8B57", border = "white",      xlab = "Iterations to converge", main = "Energy-balance solver convergence, 40 random LUT rows")

code: path_input <- system.file("input", package = "SCOPEinR") scope_options <- read.table(file.path(path_input, "setoptions.csv"), header = TRUE, sep = ",") inputLUT <- read.table(file.path(path_input, "inputs_SCOPE.csv"), header = TRUE, sep = ",")  n_samples <- 500 set.seed(11) LUT <- getLUT.SCOPE(inputLUT = inputLUT, nLUT = n_samples)  db_sims <- get.SCOPE(LUT = LUT, n.LUT = n_samples, options.SCOPE = scope_options,                       optipar = SCOPEinR::optipar2021.Pro.CX, leaf.model = "fluspect-CX",                       canopy.model = "fourSAIL", get.outputs = "ALL", get.plots = FALSE)  wl_optical <- 400:2400 n <- length(wl_optical)  band_refl <- t(sapply(db_sims, function(r) {   rfl_i <- r$data.rad$reflapp[1:n]   # reflapp is a radiance ratio -- genuinely near-zero incident irradiance   # at a handful of water-vapor/O2 absorption wavelengths makes it   # numerically unstable there in every simulation (see How-in-R-SCOPEinR.Rmd,   # Section 5). code: set.seed(1) train_idx <- sample(seq_len(n_samples), size = round(0.7 * n_samples)) test_idx  <- setdiff(seq_len(n_samples), train_idx)  r2_f   <- function(obs, pred) 1 - sum((obs - pred)^2) / sum((obs - mean(obs))^2) rmse_f <- function(obs, pred) sqrt(mean((obs - pred)^2))  invert_trait <- function(trait) {   ml_data <- data.frame(band_refl, y = LUT[[trait]])   rf <- randomForest(y ~ ., data = ml_data[train_idx, ], ntree = 300)   pred <- predict(rf, ml_data[-train_idx, ])   obs  <- ml_data$y[-train_idx]   list(obs = obs, pred = pred, R2 = r2_f(obs, pred), RMSE = rmse_f(obs, pred)) }

text: greenness index simple NDVI-like ratio computed directly reflapp (sensor convolution needed comparison) – red (670nm) vs. NIR (800nm) reflectance, contrast NDVI uses:
code: wl_optical <- 400:2400 n <- length(wl_optical) i670 <- which(wl_optical == 670) i800 <- which(wl_optical == 800)  get_finite <- function(rfl_i) {   bad <- !is.finite(rfl_i)   if (any(bad)) rfl_i[bad] <- approx(wl_optical[!bad], rfl_i[!bad], xout = wl_optical[bad])$y   rfl_i }  df <- data.frame(   Actot = sapply(db_sims, function(r) r$data.fluxes$Actot),   EoutF = sapply(db_sims, function(r) r$data.rad$EoutF),   NDVI  = sapply(db_sims, function(r) {     rfl_i <- get_finite(r$data.rad$reflapp[1:n])     (rfl_i[i800] - rfl_i[i670]) / (rfl_i[i800] + rfl_i[i670])   }) ) op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) plot(df$NDVI, df$Actot, pch = 19, col = "#2E8B57", xlab = "NDVI-like index", ylab = "Actot") plot(df$EoutF, df$Actot, pch = 19, col = "#B2182B", xlab = "EoutF (SIF)", ylab = "Actot") par(op)

what: 3. Three models: greenness alone, SIF alone, both together
title: Does SIF add information about photosynthesis beyond greenness?
text: individual-predictor models weak held-test set – R² zero NDVI alone SIF alone, meaning neither beats simply predicting mean Actot every time. real, useful negative result: across LUT every trait varies (leaf biochemistry, LAI, geometry – just one driving Actot directly, Vcmax25), one predictor alone swamped nuisance variation, confounding effect inversion-scope article found single-trait retrieval kind full-range LUT. Combining NDVI SIF (R² > 0 first time) actual result worth taking away: even weak, individually-unreliable SIF signal adds real information top NDVI NDVI alone doesn’t carry – consistent literature’s claim direction, even though absolute retrieval skill modest. larger LUT, one isolates Vcmax25 nuisance traits (--Python-SCOPEinR.ipynb’s small perturbation-LUT ), expected show effect clearly deliberately full-range, information-poor setup.
